angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 612,216 km at 72.45 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.8029 +/- 0.0584 mas (same row, RUWE 2.84): 72.45 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.88 solar radii from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: radius 0.88 solar radii (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684): 612,216 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9 solar masses from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: mass 0.9 solar masses (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5291 K from SIMBAD, measurements of BD-16 351 (table mesFe_h), row of 2024A&A...690A..97C: Teff (https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/EEM_dwarf_UBVIJHK_colors_Teff.txt). Spin inclination 42 degrees and rotation period 3.21 d from Folsom et al., arXiv:1601.00684, Table 2: rotation period 3.21 d and an axis 42 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with (https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00684). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: SIMBAD, measurements of BD-16 351 (table mesFe_h), row of 2024A&A...690A..97C: Teff (https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/EEM_dwarf_UBVIJHK_colors_Teff.txt)
